```{=html}
<!--
Mirrors usgs_veg.qmd's structure, adapted for veg_final.xlsx's own
column shapes. Chains onto elev_z_flux.csv (elevation_and_z_star.qmd's
output) -- reads it, joins veg_final.xlsx on top, writes
elev_z_veg_flux_long.csv.

THIS FILE'S OUTPUT IS NOT AN INPUT TO master_analysis_flagtier.qmd,
BY DESIGN, PERMANENTLY -- not a placeholder pending a future decision.
master_analysis_flagtier.qmd keeps reading elev_z_flux.csv (elevation
only) directly, unchanged. Multi-species fan-out means this table has
more rows than one-per-flux-observation, so feeding it into tiering
would silently inflate every Flux-based statistic tiering produces.
elev_z_veg_flux_long.csv exists as its own parallel object for
species-level visualization (SAPA_thesis/SPFO_thesis-style breakdowns),
separate from the core tiering pipeline -- the same relationship
usgs_elev_veg_flux_long.csv has to master_analysis_usgs.Rmd's sed_usgs.

MULTI-SPECIES ROWS ARE KEPT INTENTIONALLY, NOT A PENDING DECISION.
Confirmed: you want every species preserved per plot for per-species
visualization (the SAPA_thesis/SPFO_thesis-style breakdowns already in
veg.Rmd). So this file, like usgs_veg.qmd, joins in long form on
purpose -- "_long" in the filename means "one row per species per flux
observation, by design," not "not yet collapsed."

CONSEQUENCE THAT STILL MATTERS: any Flux-based aggregate (mean flux,
tier statistics, a model using Flux as the response) computed directly
on this long-form table will double- or triple-count Flux at any plot
with multiple species logged. That's fine for veg-focused visualization
(you want to see Flux the ggplot ends up faceting/coloring by Species,
where the repeated Flux rows are correct/expected), but NOT fine for
anything computing Flux summary statistics or fitting a Flux ~ ...
model without filtering to one species first (or otherwise handling
the duplication). Keep both use cases in mind: this table is for
species-level visualization, not a drop-in replacement for
elev_z_flux.csv in a model.
-->
```

```{r, load elevation-joined flux data and raw veg data}
usgs_thesis <- read_excel("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\usgs_thesis.xlsx", 
                          col_types = "text"
                          )

thesis_veg_raw <- read_csv("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\veg_final.csv")
```

```{r, clean thesis veg}
# Site letter codes -> full names, same mapping as
# master_analysis_cleanup.Rmd's own case_when. str_squish first --
# "S " has a trailing space in the raw file.
# CHANGED: Date is now parsed and kept as the join key (replaces the
# old Month+Year approximate match) -- confirmed every veg survey Date
# exactly matches a Date.removed.from.field value in the flux data, so
# this is a real same-day match, not a same-month approximation.

thesis_veg <- thesis_veg_raw |>
  mutate(
    Site = str_squish(as.character(Site)),
    Site = case_when(
      Site == "C" ~ "CorteMadera",
      Site == "G" ~ "GiantMarsh",
      Site == "B" ~ "Buck'sLanding",
      Site == "S" ~ "SanPablo",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    Date    = as.Date(Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y"),
    AvgHt   = ifelse(is.na(AvgHt), 0, AvgHt),
    MaxHt   = ifelse(is.na(MaxHt), 0, MaxHt),
    Cover   = as.numeric(Cover),
    Season  = str_squish(Season),
    Site    = str_remove_all(Site, " "),
    Year    = str_squish(as.character(Year)),   # kept for reference, redundant with Date now
    Month   = str_to_title(str_squish(Month)),  # kept for grouping/plots, no longer used in the join
    Year  = str_squish(as.character(Year)),     # kept for reference, redundant with Date now
    Tran    = str_extract(`Plot.ID`, "^[A-Za-z]+"),
    Dist    = as.numeric(str_extract(`Plot.ID`, "[0-9.]+$"))
  )

  separate(PlotID, into = c("Tran", "Dist"), sep = "-", remove = FALSE) |>
  mutate(Dist = as.numeric(Dist))

str(thesis_veg)

# Confirms the (intentional) multi-species fan-out before it hits the
# join -- now keyed by exact Date instead of Month/Year.
thesis_veg |>
  count(Site, Tran, Dist, Date) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  nrow()
```

```{r, key the flux data to match}
# Month is derived fresh here from Date.removed.from.field rather than
# trusted off elev_z_flux.csv -- unlike usgs_veg.qmd (which could
# confirm master_usgs.csv already carries a clean Month column),
# there's no confirmation master_thesis.csv/elev_z_flux.csv has one at
# all (master_analysis_cleanup.Rmd's visible code never derives it).
# Deriving it locally keeps this file self-contained and avoids
# assuming a column exists sight-unseen -- same defensive choice
# usgs_thesis_merge.qmd already makes for both sides of that merge.
study_month_levels <- c("July", "August", "September", "October",
                         "November", "December", "January", "February",
                         "March", "April", "May", "June")

usgs_thesis <- usgs_thesis |>
  mutate(
    Site  = str_squish(as.character(Site)),
    Tran  = str_squish(as.character(Tran)),
    Dist  = as.numeric(as.character(Dist)),
    Year  = str_squish(as.character(Year)),
    Month = as.character(month(Date.removed.from.field, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE))
  )
```

```{r, filter to veg-sampled rows only}
  
  # Restricts the long-form join down to only the flux rows that actually
  # have a matching vegetation record, rather than every flux row across
  # the full campaign (elev_z_veg_flux_long.csv intentionally keeps all
  # of those -- see file header). This filtered version is for RQ3,
  # where we only want rows collected at points/months veg was actually
  # sampled, not NA-padded rows from months it wasn't.
  elev_z_veg_flux_sampled <- elev_z_veg_flux_long |>
    filter(!is.na(Species))
  
  nrow(elev_z_veg_flux_sampled)   # should match the has_veg = TRUE count below
  
  readr::write_csv(elev_z_veg_flux_sampled, "C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\elev_z_veg_flux_sampled.csv")

  
```

```{r, diagnostics}
nrow(elev_z_flux_keyed)
nrow(elev_z_veg_flux_long)
nrow(elev_z_veg_flux_long) - nrow(elev_z_flux_keyed)   # rows added by species fan-out, expected and fine here

# Coverage -- veg_final.xlsx only covers Feb/June 2026 so far (this
# season's survey isn't complete), so most flux rows across the full
# ~12-month campaign are expected to show has_veg = FALSE. Not a bug --
# same kind of sparsity as the USGS veg join, just from an
# still-in-progress collection rather than a fixed 3-visit design.
elev_z_flux_keyed |>
  left_join(
    thesis_veg |> distinct(Site, Tran, Dist, Date) |> mutate(has_veg = TRUE),
    by = c("Site", "Tran", "Dist", "Date.removed.from.field" = "Date")
  ) |>
  count(has_veg)
```
